page: Amazon Web Services c8in.2xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized server instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. Utilizing the x86_64 instruction set, the instance runs on an Intel processor with a sustained clock frequency of 3.9 GHz. Its execution topology provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading. System memory is sized at 16.0 GB, establishing a compute-dense 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are absent, aligning system resources purely toward general processor throughput.

Storage and connectivity rely on AWS Nitro architecture offloading. The c8in.2xlarge does not include local disk storage, meaning root volumes and persistent storage require Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) attachments. Network performance is designed for high-throughput demands, offering a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps alongside dedicated EBS optimization to prevent traffic contention between block storage operations and application networking. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires private subnet allocation or managed gateway routing.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the c8in.2xlarge delivers a high ratio of dedicated processing capacity and network throughput per unit of RAM. The operational tradeoff centers on the lack of onboard storage and the strict 2.0 GB per vCPU memory profile, which precludes memory-intensive databases or workloads requiring ultra-low latency ephemeral local scratch space. Consequently, this instance configuration fits compute-intensive workloads that generate moderate memory footprints and require consistent network transport, such as CI/CD runners, distributed batch processing nodes, stateless web and application serving, and network appliance routing.
description: Amazon Web Services c8in.2xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it incorporates an Intel processor operating at 3.9 GHz with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores and two threads per core. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual processor. Storage is entirely decoupled, with no local NVMe or SSD drives provided, necessitating external Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent and root disk operations. For high-throughput I/O scenarios, the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps along with dedicated EBS optimization. The instance does not include hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Its compute-dense configuration suits workloads requiring consistent high-frequency CPU cycles alongside reliable network throughput, such as distributed compute nodes, batch processing, application servers, and network-bound microservices.
